events_run1: A ruler cries out for everyone else to leave the room.
Alone with his brothers, the ruler reveals who he is.
He weeps so loudly that the household of the king hears.
His brothers are too troubled to answer him.
He tells them to come near and says he is the brother they sold.
He tells them to bring their father to live near him during the famine.
He embraces his younger brother and weeps, then kisses all his brothers, and they talk with him.
The king hears of it and is pleased, and tells the ruler to send the brothers home for their father and families.
The ruler gives the brothers wagons, supplies for the journey, and changes of clothing.
He gives his younger brother silver and extra clothing.
He sends his father ten donkeys loaded with goods and ten with food.
He sends the brothers away, telling them not to quarrel on the way.
events_run2: A ruler cries out for everyone else to leave the room.
The ruler reveals himself to his brothers and weeps so loudly that the household hears.
The brothers are too troubled to answer him.
The ruler tells them to come near and explains that they sold him but that God sent him ahead to save lives.
He tells them to hurry back and bring their father to live near him during the famine.
He embraces his younger brother and weeps, then kisses all his brothers, and they talk with him.
The king hears the news and is pleased, and tells the ruler to send his brothers to fetch their father and households.
The ruler gives his brothers wagons, provisions, and clothing, with extra silver and clothing for his younger brother.
The ruler sends his father gifts of animals laden with goods and food.
The ruler sends his brothers away, telling them not to quarrel on the road.
The brothers return to their father and tell him the ruler is alive.
The father does not believe them until he sees the wagons, and then he decides to go see his son.

events_run1: A king finished building the temple and his own house.
God appeared to the king a second time and promised to establish his throne if he stayed faithful.
After twenty years of building, the king gave twenty cities to a neighboring king who had supplied him with timber and gold.
The neighboring king came to see the cities and was displeased with them.
The neighboring king called the region a name of disapproval.
The neighboring king sent the king a large amount of gold.
The king raised a levy of labor to build the temple, his house, and fortified cities.
A foreign ruler had earlier captured a city, burned it, and given it to his daughter, the king's wife.
The king rebuilt that city and many other cities for storage, chariots, and horsemen.
The king forced the remaining foreign peoples into bondservice but did not enslave his own people.
The ruler's daughter moved into the house the king built for her.
The king offered sacrifices three times a year, and sent a fleet of ships whose crews fetched gold from a distant land.
events_run2: A king finished building the temple and his own house.
God appeared to the king a second time and spoke to him about his prayer.
After twenty years of building, the king gave twenty cities to a neighboring king who had supplied him with timber and gold.
The neighboring king came out to see the cities and was displeased with them.
The neighboring king named the region a name of scorn.
The neighboring king sent a large amount of gold to the king.
The king raised a labor levy to build the temple, his house, and fortified cities.
A foreign ruler had earlier captured and burned a city and given it to his daughter, the king's wife.
The king rebuilt that city and many other cities for storage, chariots, and horsemen.
The king forced the remaining foreign peoples into bondservice.
The king's wife moved from the old city to the house he had built for her.
The king offered sacrifices three times a year and finished the temple.

events_run1: A new king began to rule the northern kingdom and did evil.
God let the enemy king and his son oppress the kingdom.
The king begged God for help, and God sent a saviour who freed the people from the enemy.
The enemy had destroyed most of the army, leaving only a few horsemen, chariots and footmen.
The king died and was buried, and his son became king.
The new king also did evil and fought against the king of the southern kingdom.
That king died and was buried, and another man took his throne.
A prophet fell sick, and the king came and wept over him.
At the prophet's command, the king took a bow and arrows, opened the window, and shot an arrow eastward.
The king struck the ground with arrows only three times, and the angry prophet said he would defeat the enemy only three times.
The prophet died and was buried.
A dead man thrown into the prophet's tomb touched his bones and came back to life.
events_run2: A new king began to reign over the northern kingdom and did evil.
God's anger led to the people being handed over to a foreign king and his son.
The king prayed, and God heard him and gave the people a deliverer.
The people escaped foreign rule, but the foreign king had left the army almost destroyed.
The king died and was buried, and his son became king.
The new king did evil and fought against the neighboring kingdom, then died and was buried.
The king visited the dying prophet and wept over him.
The prophet had the king take a bow and arrows, open a window, and shoot an arrow as a sign of deliverance.
The king struck the ground with arrows only three times, and the prophet was angry.
The prophet died and was buried.
Raiders invaded, and a dead man's burial party threw his body into the prophet's tomb, and he came back to life when he touched the bones.
The king defeated the foreign enemy three times and recovered the lost cities.

events_run1: The king gave the house of his executed enemy to the queen.
The queen's cousin came before the king, and the king gave him his ring.
The queen set her cousin over the enemy's house.
The queen fell at the king's feet in tears and begged him to undo the enemy's plot against her people.
The king held out the golden sceptre, and she stood and asked that the letters of the plot be reversed.
The king told her and her cousin to write for their people in his name and seal it with his ring.
The king's scribes were called and wrote out the cousin's orders to every province.
Riders on horses, mules and camels carried the letters out, hurried by the king's command.
The letters allowed the people to gather and defend themselves against any who attacked them on one appointed day.
The cousin left the king in royal robes and a golden crown, and the city rejoiced.
The people held feasts and celebrated in every province and city.
Many people of the land became part of the people, because fear of them had fallen on others.
events_run2: The king gave the dead enemy's house to the queen.
The queen presented her relative to the king, and the king gave him his ring.
The queen set her relative over the enemy's house.
The queen fell at the king's feet in tears and begged him to undo the enemy's plot against her people.
The king held out the golden sceptre, and she stood and asked him to reverse the enemy's letters.
The king told her and her relative to write for their people in his name and seal it with his ring.
The king's scribes were called and wrote out the new decree in every language to all the provinces.
Messengers on horses, mules and camels rode out with the letters, allowing the people to gather and defend themselves on one appointed day.
The decree was given in the palace.
The queen's relative left the king in royal robes and a gold crown.
The city rejoiced, and the people held feasts in every province.
Many people of the land became Jews out of fear.

events_run1: A man of a tribe took forbidden spoils, and the people's God became angry.
A leader sent men from the city to view another city.
The men viewed the city and returned, advising that only a few thousand men go up.
About three thousand men went up and fled before the city's men.
The city's men killed about thirty-six of them while chasing them from the gate.
The leader tore his clothes and lay on his face before the ark until evening, with the elders putting dust on their heads.
God told the leader that the people had sinned and must be sanctified, and that the guilty one would be found by lot.
The next morning the leader brought the people forward by tribe, family, and household, and the man was singled out.
The man confessed that he had coveted and taken a garment, silver, and gold, and hidden them in his tent.
Messengers ran to the tent and found the goods, and brought them to the leader and the people.
The people took the man, his family, his animals, his belongings, and the goods to a valley.
The people stoned the man and his family, burned them, and raised a great heap of stones over them.
events_run2: A man of the people took forbidden spoils, and the people's God became angry.
A leader sent men to view a nearby city.
The men returned and advised sending only a small force.
About three thousand men went up and were driven off in flight.
The defenders chased them and killed about thirty-six.
The leader and the elders tore their clothes and lay on the ground before the ark until evening.
God told the leader to rise and ordered the people to purify themselves.
The next morning the leader brought the people forward by tribe, family, and household until the guilty man was chosen.
The guilty man confessed that he had taken a garment, silver, and gold and hidden them in his tent.
Messengers ran to the tent, found the goods, and brought them to the leader.
The people took the man, his family, his animals, his goods, and his tent to a valley.
The people stoned and burned them, raised a heap of stones over them, and God's anger turned away.

events_run1: A chief warrior raised his spear against eight hundred men and killed them at one time.
A warrior fought a gathered enemy army until his hand was weary and clung to his sword, after the other men had fled.
The people returned after him only to take the spoil of a great victory.
When the enemy gathered in a field of lentils and the people fled, another warrior stood in the field, defended it, and killed the enemy.
Three chief warriors went down to the king at a cave during harvest time while an enemy troop camped in a valley.
The king, in a stronghold, longed for water from the well by the gate of his home town, which an enemy garrison held.
The three warriors broke through the enemy army, drew water from the well, and brought it to the king.
The king refused to drink the water and poured it out to God.
Another warrior raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them.
A valiant man's son killed two strong men of a neighboring land and killed a lion in a pit in snowy weather.
He went down with a staff against a spear-carrying foreigner, took the spear from his hand, and killed him with it.
The king set that warrior over his guard.
events_run2: A chief warrior raised his spear against eight hundred men and killed them at one time.
A warrior fought the enemy army until his hand was weary and clung to his sword, and the people returned after him only to take spoil.
Another warrior stood in the middle of a field of lentils while the people fled, defended it, and killed the enemy.
Three of the chief warriors went down to the king at a cave in harvest time while an enemy troop camped in a valley.
The king, in a stronghold while the enemy held his home town, longed for water from the town's well.
The three warriors broke through the enemy camp, drew water from the well, and brought it to the king.
The king refused to drink the water and poured it out as an offering.
Another warrior raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them.
A valiant man's son killed two strong men, and killed a lion in a pit in snowy weather.
He went down with only a staff against a tall foreign man holding a spear, took the spear from him, and killed him with it.
The king set that warrior over his guard.

events_run1: A young man was brought to a foreign land and sold to an officer of the king.
The officer put the young man in charge of his whole household.
The household and fields prospered because of him.
The officer's wife asked the young man to lie with her, and he refused.
She kept asking him day after day, and he kept refusing.
One day, when no one else was in the house, she caught him by his garment.
He left his garment in her hand and fled outside.
She called the household men and falsely accused him of attacking her.
She kept the garment until her husband came home and told him the same false story.
The angry officer put the young man into the king's prison.
The prison keeper favored him and put all the prisoners in his charge.
events_run2: A young man was taken down to a foreign land and sold to an officer of the king.
The officer made the young man overseer of his house and put everything in his care.
The officer's household and fields prospered because of the young man.
The officer's wife asked the young man to lie with her, and he refused.
She kept asking him day after day, and he kept refusing.
One day, when no other men were in the house, she caught him by his garment.
He left his garment in her hand and fled outside.
She called the men of her house and falsely said he had tried to attack her.
She kept the garment beside her until her husband came home.
She told her husband the same false story.
The husband grew angry and put the young man into the prison for the king's prisoners.
The keeper of the prison put all the prisoners in the young man's care.

events_run1: A governor arrived in his province and three days later went up to the capital city.
The chief priest and Jewish leaders accused a prisoner before him and asked that the prisoner be sent to the city, planning an ambush to kill him on the way.
The governor refused and said the prisoner would stay in the coastal city, and told the accusers to come down with him.
After more than ten days, the governor went down to the coastal city and the next day sat on the judgment seat and ordered the prisoner brought in.
The accusers from the capital stood around him and made many serious charges they could not prove.
The prisoner denied any offense against the law, the temple, or the emperor.
The governor, wanting to please the accusers, asked the prisoner whether he would be tried in the capital city.
The prisoner refused and appealed to the emperor.
The governor conferred with his council and granted the appeal.
After some days a king and his sister arrived at the coastal city to greet the governor.
The governor told the king about the prisoner's case, which he had inherited from the previous governor.
The king asked to hear the prisoner, and the next day he arrived with great pomp and the prisoner was brought before the assembly.
events_run2: A new governor arrived in the province and three days later went up to the capital city.
The chief priest and Jewish leaders accused a prisoner to him and asked that he be sent to the city, planning to ambush and kill him on the way.
The governor refused and said the prisoner would stay in the coastal city, where he would soon return.
After more than ten days, the governor went down to the coastal city.
The next day he sat on the judgment seat and had the prisoner brought in.
The accusers from the capital stood around and made many serious charges they could not prove.
The prisoner denied any offense, and the governor, wanting to please the accusers, asked whether he would be tried in the capital.
The prisoner refused and appealed to the emperor.
The governor conferred with his council and agreed to send him to the emperor.
Some days later a king and his sister arrived in the coastal city to greet the governor.
The governor told the king about the prisoner's case, and the king asked to hear him.
The next day the king arrived with great pomp, and the prisoner was brought before the assembly.

events_run1: An old man made his chief servant swear to find a wife for his son from the man's own relatives, not from the local people.
The servant took ten camels and traveled to the city of the man's relatives.
He made the camels kneel by a well in the evening and prayed for a sign.
A young woman came to the well and gave him water, then offered to water all his camels too.
The servant gave her a gold earring and two gold bracelets and asked whose daughter she was.
She said she was the daughter of the man's relative and offered him lodging.
The servant bowed and worshipped, and the young woman ran home to tell her family.
Her brother ran to the well and welcomed the servant into the house, where the camels were tended and the servant's feet were washed.
The servant refused to eat until he had told his errand, then explained his mission and the well.
Her father and brother agreed she should go, and the servant gave gifts to her and her family.
The next morning the family asked her to stay, but she agreed to leave at once, and they sent her off with her nurse and blessed her.
She rode back on a camel, met the son in the field, covered herself with a veil, and became his wife.
events_run2: An old man makes his chief servant swear to find a wife for his son from the man's own kindred, not from the local people.
The servant takes ten camels and travels to the distant city.
He makes the camels kneel by a well in the evening and prays for a sign.
A young woman comes to the well and gives him water, then draws water for all his camels.
The servant gives her a gold earring and two gold bracelets and asks whose daughter she is.
She says she is from his master's family and offers lodging, and the servant worships.
She runs home and tells her family, and her brother hurries out to bring the servant in.
The servant is welcomed into the house, and he refuses to eat until he has told his errand.
He tells the family the whole story, and they agree that she should go with him.
He gives gifts to the young woman and her family, and they spend the night.
In the morning her family asks her to stay, but she agrees to leave at once.
She travels with the servant and meets his master's son, who takes her as his wife.

events_run1: A dying king charged his son to follow God's ways and to deal with certain men after his death.
The old king died and was buried in the city.
His son took the throne, and his kingdom was firmly established.
The king's older brother asked the king's mother to request a young woman as his wife.
The king's mother went to the king, and he welcomed her and seated her at his right hand.
She asked that the young woman be given to the king's brother, and the king angrily refused.
The king swore the brother would die, and had him killed.
The king banished a priest to his own fields and removed him from the priesthood.
A general who had backed the brother fled to the altar, and the king had him killed there.
The king appointed a new army commander and a new priest.
The king ordered a man to stay in the city on pain of death, and the man agreed.
After three years the man left the city to retrieve his runaway servants, and the king had him killed on his return.
events_run2: A dying king gives his son final instructions about the people he should deal with.
The king dies and is buried in the city.
The son sits on the throne and his kingdom is firmly established.
The new king's older brother asks the king's mother to request a wife for him.
The mother goes to the king, who honors her and seats her at his right hand.
She makes the request, and the king angrily refuses and swears the brother will die.
The king sends a man who kills the brother.
The king removes a priest from office and sends him away to his own fields.
A commander who had backed the brother flees to the altar, and the king orders him killed there.
The man kills the commander, who is buried at his home in the wilderness.
The king gives the dead commander's post and the priest's post to new men.
The king orders another man to stay in the city on pain of death, and the man agrees.

events_run1: A king defeated his old enemies and took control of their land.
He defeated a neighboring people, put many to death, and made the rest his servants who paid tribute.
He fought a rival king who was trying to restore his border at a great river.
He captured many of the rival king's chariots, horsemen, and foot soldiers, and crippled most of the chariot horses.
Another people came to help the rival king, and the king killed twenty-two thousand of them.
He placed garrisons in their land, and they became his servants who paid tribute.
He took gold shields and a great amount of brass from the rival king's servants and cities, and brought them to the capital city.
A faraway king, hearing of the victory, sent his son with silver, gold, and brass gifts to bless him.
The king dedicated those gifts, along with the spoil from all the nations he had conquered, to God.
He returned from defeating eighteen thousand men in a valley and gained a famous name.
He placed garrisons throughout another land, and its people became his servants.
events_run2: A king defeated a neighboring people and took control of their territory.
He defeated another people, put many to death, and made the rest his servants who paid tribute.
He defeated a rival king as that king went to restore his border at a river.
He captured many chariots, horsemen, and soldiers, and crippled most of the chariot horses.
Allied soldiers from a nearby city came to help the rival king, and the king killed many of them.
He placed garrisons in their land, and they became his servants and paid tribute.
He brought golden shields to the capital city and took much brass from the rival king's cities.
A distant king heard of the victory and sent his son with silver, gold and brass gifts to congratulate him.
The king dedicated those gifts, with the other spoil from conquered nations, to God.
He won renown by defeating a large army in a valley.
He placed garrisons throughout another land, and its people became his servants.
He reigned over his whole nation and appointed officers, priests, a scribe and a recorder.

events_run1: An enemy people gathered their armies to fight a neighboring nation.
A foreign ruler told a fugitive warrior he would march out to battle with him, and made him his bodyguard.
The king camped his army opposite the enemy, and became terrified when he saw their host.
The king asked God for guidance, but received no answer.
The king told his servants to find a woman who spoke with spirits.
The king disguised himself and went to her by night with two men.
The woman feared a trap, but the king swore she would not be punished.
At the king's request, the woman called up the dead prophet.
The woman saw the prophet, realized who the visitor was, and cried out.
The prophet told the king that God had left him, the kingdom would go to another, and he and his sons would die in battle the next day.
The king collapsed to the ground in fear, weak from not having eaten.
The woman and servants persuaded him to eat, and she baked bread for them, and then they left that night.
events_run2: A foreign people gathered their armies to fight the people of a rival nation.
A foreign ruler told a fugitive warrior he would go with him to battle, and made him his permanent bodyguard.
The king gathered his people and camped opposite the enemy army.
The king grew afraid when he saw the enemy host.
The king asked God for guidance, but received no answer.
The king told his servants to find a woman who spoke with spirits.
The king disguised himself and went by night with two men to the woman in a village.
The woman, fearing for her life, was reassured by the king's oath, and then raised the dead prophet at his request.
The woman cried out in fear when she saw the prophet, recognizing the king.
The king bowed to the ground before the prophet's spirit.
The prophet told the king that he would lose his kingdom and that he and his sons would die in battle the next day.
The king collapsed in fear, then was persuaded to eat, and the woman killed a calf and baked bread for him and his servants.

events_run1: A king of a great empire attacked a kingdom, and its king served him for three years.
The king of the kingdom then rebelled against the empire's king.
Bands of raiders from neighboring peoples were sent against the kingdom to destroy it.
The king of the kingdom died, and his son became king.
The king of Egypt stayed in his own land because the empire had taken all his territory.
The young new king began to reign and did evil for three months.
The empire's servants came against the city and besieged it.
The empire's king came to the city, and the kingdom's king surrendered to him with his mother, servants, and officials.
The empire's king took the treasures of the temple and the palace and cut up the gold vessels.
He carried away thousands of captives, including the king, the royal family, soldiers, and craftsmen, leaving only the poorest people.
The empire's king made the captive king's uncle the new king and changed his name.
The new king later rebelled against the empire's king.
events_run2: A king of a great empire attacked a kingdom, and its king served him for three years.
The king of the kingdom then rebelled against him.
Raiding bands from neighboring peoples were sent against the kingdom to destroy it.
The rebel king died, and his son became king.
The king of the great empire took all the land that had belonged to the king of Egypt, so Egypt's king stayed home.
The young new king began to reign at eighteen and did evil.
The empire's servants came up against the city and besieged it.
The empire's king came to the besieged city himself.
The young king surrendered to him with his mother, servants, princes and officers.
The empire's king took the treasures of the temple and the palace and cut up the gold vessels.
He carried away the city's leaders, warriors and craftsmen as captives, leaving only the poorest people.
He made the young king's uncle king in his place and renamed him, and the uncle later rebelled against the empire.

events_run1: A new king began to rule over the northern kingdom.
A powerful foreign king attacked him, and he became that king's servant and paid him gifts.
The foreign king discovered the northern king had sent messengers to another kingdom and had stopped paying tribute.
The foreign king seized the northern king and put him in prison.
The foreign king invaded the whole land and besieged the capital city for three years.
The foreign king captured the city and carried the people away to his own land.
He settled the captives in distant cities and regions.
The foreign king brought people from several other lands and settled them in the northern cities.
The new settlers did not honor the God of the land, and lions came among them and killed some.
The settlers told the foreign king about the lions.
The foreign king ordered that one of the exiled priests be sent back to teach them.
A priest returned, lived in a city, and taught the settlers how to honor God, though each nation also made its own gods.
events_run2: A new king began to rule over the northern kingdom.
A powerful foreign king attacked him, and he became that king's servant and paid him gifts.
The new king secretly sent messengers to another land's king and stopped paying the yearly gifts.
The foreign king discovered the plot and bound the king in prison.
The foreign king invaded the whole land and besieged the capital city for three years.
The foreign king captured the city and carried the people away to distant lands.
The foreign king brought settlers from other nations to live in the emptied cities.
The settlers did not honor the God of the land, and lions were sent among them and killed some.
The settlers told the foreign king about the lions and why they thought it was happening.
The foreign king ordered that one of the exiled priests be sent back to teach them.
A priest came, lived in a nearby town, and taught them how to honor God.
Each nation still made its own gods and worshipped them alongside God.

events_run1: A famine continued, and the family ate all the grain they had brought from the foreign land.
The father told his sons to go again and buy a little food.
One son reminded him that the ruler would not see them unless the youngest brother came along.
The father reluctantly agreed to send the youngest brother and told them to take gifts and double money.
The sons traveled to the foreign land with the gifts, the money, and the youngest brother, and stood before the ruler.
The ruler saw the youngest brother and ordered his house steward to bring the men to his house for a noon meal.
The frightened brothers were taken to the ruler's house and explained to the steward about the money found in their sacks.
The steward told them not to fear, said he had received their money, and brought out their imprisoned brother.
The steward gave them water to wash their feet and fed their animals.
When the ruler came home, the brothers gave him the gifts and bowed to the ground before him.
The ruler asked about their father, saw his youngest brother, and blessed him.
The ruler went to his chamber and wept, then washed his face and returned to order the meal served.
events_run2: The famine continued and the family ran out of the grain they had brought from the foreign land.
The father told his sons to go back and buy more food.
One son promised to guarantee the youngest brother's safety, and the father reluctantly agreed to send him.
The father sent the sons with gifts, double money, and the money returned in their sacks.
The brothers traveled to the foreign land and stood before the ruler.
The ruler saw the youngest brother and ordered his steward to bring the men to his house for a meal.
The frightened brothers spoke to the steward at the door and explained the money found in their sacks.
The steward told them not to fear and brought out their imprisoned brother to them.
The steward gave them water to wash their feet and fed their donkeys.
The ruler came home, and the brothers gave him the gifts and bowed to the ground.
The ruler asked about their father, saw his youngest brother, and left the room to weep.
The ruler washed his face, returned, and served the meal, giving the youngest brother five times as much as the others.

events_run1: God creates light and separates it from the darkness, calling them Day and Night.
God makes a firmament to divide the waters above from the waters below.
God gathers the waters into one place so dry land appears, naming them Earth and Seas.
The earth brings forth grass, plants and fruit trees.
God makes the sun, moon and stars in the sky to give light and mark time.
God creates sea creatures and birds and blesses them to multiply.
God makes the land animals, cattle and creeping things.
God creates man and woman in his own image.
God blesses them and gives them rule over all living things.
God gives plants to man and the animals for food.
God sees all that he has made and calls it very good.
events_run2: God creates light and separates it from the darkness, making the first day and night.
God makes a firmament to divide the waters above from the waters below.
God gathers the waters into seas and lets dry land appear.
The earth brings forth grass, plants, and fruit trees.
God makes the sun, moon, and stars to give light and mark the days, seasons, and years.
God makes sea creatures and birds, and blesses them to multiply.
God makes the land animals, cattle, and creeping things.
God creates man and woman in his own image.
God blesses them and gives them rule over all living things.
God gives plants and herbs as food for people and animals.
God sees all that he has made and calls it very good.

events_run1: Two missionaries and their companion traveled through two towns and came to a city with a synagogue.
The missionary went into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews from the scriptures for three sabbath days.
Some Jews, many devout Greeks, and several leading women believed and joined them.
The unbelieving Jews, moved by envy, gathered a mob of bad men and set the city in an uproar.
The mob attacked a believer's house, failed to find the missionaries, and dragged the believer and some brethren before the city rulers.
The rulers took security from the believer and the others and let them go.
The brethren sent the missionaries away by night to another city, where they went into the synagogue.
The people there received the message eagerly, searched the scriptures daily, and many believed.
The unbelieving Jews from the first city came and stirred up the crowds, so the brethren sent the missionary off toward the sea.
Those escorting him brought him to a great city, then left to carry his command for his companions to come quickly.
While waiting, the missionary was troubled by the city's idols and argued in the synagogue and the marketplace.
Philosophers brought him to a hill, where he preached about an altar to an unknown god, and some mocked while a few believed.
events_run2: Two travelers pass through two towns and arrive at a city with a synagogue.
One of them reasons with the people in the synagogue from the scriptures for three sabbaths.
Some Jews, many devout Greeks, and many leading women believe and join them.
The unbelieving Jews, moved by envy, gather a mob of worthless men and set the city in an uproar.
The mob attacks a man's house, looking for the travelers.
Not finding them, the mob drags the host and some believers before the city rulers and accuses them.
The rulers take security from the host and the others and let them go.
The believers send the two travelers away by night to another town, where they enter the synagogue.
The people there receive the message eagerly and many believe.
The unbelieving Jews from the first city arrive and stir up the crowds, so the believers send the traveler on toward the sea and then to a great city.
In the great city he argues in the synagogue and market, and philosophers bring him to a hill to explain his teaching.
He speaks to them, and some mock, some want to hear more, and a few join him.

events_run1: The priest, the leader, and the tribal heads divided the land of the promised country by lot among nine and a half tribes.
The Levites received no share of land, only cities to live in with pasture.
The men of one tribe came to the leader at the camp.
A veteran of the earlier spy mission stepped forward to speak to the leader.
He recalled how a prophet had sent him at age forty to spy out the land.
He recalled how the prophet had sworn to give him the land he had walked on.
He said he was now eighty-five and as strong for war as he had been then.
He asked the leader for the mountain, where giants lived in great walled cities.
The leader blessed him.
The leader gave him the city as an inheritance.
The city, once named for a giant ancestor, became his family's possession.
The land had rest from war.
events_run2: A priest, a leader, and the tribal heads divided the land by lot among nine and a half tribes.
The Levites received only cities to live in, with pastureland, instead of a share of the land.
The people divided the land as they had been commanded.
Men of one tribe came to the leader at the camp.
An old, faithful man among them reminded the leader of a promise a prophet had made to him long before.
He recalled how the prophet had sent him to spy out the land, and how he alone, with one other, had followed God fully while the other spies discouraged the people.
He said he was still as strong as when he was sent out, and asked for the mountain where the giants lived.
The leader blessed him.
The leader gave him the mountain city as his inheritance.
The land had rest from war.

events_run1: A woman told her daughter-in-law to wash, dress, and go to the threshing floor where a kinsman was working.
The younger woman went down to the floor and did as she was told.
After the man had eaten and drunk, he lay down at the end of the grain heap.
She came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
At midnight the man woke afraid and found a woman at his feet.
She told him who she was and asked him to spread his covering over her as a near kinsman.
He blessed her and promised to act for her, saying a nearer kinsman had the first claim.
She lay at his feet until morning and rose before anyone could recognize her.
He measured six measures of barley, laid them on her veil, and she went into the city.
Her mother-in-law asked who she was, and she told her all that the man had done.
She showed the barley he had given her.
Her mother-in-law told her to wait, since the man would settle the matter that day.
events_run2: A woman tells her daughter-in-law to wash, dress, and go to the threshing floor to find a relative.
The younger woman agrees and goes down to the threshing floor.
The man eats and drinks, then lies down at the end of a heap of grain.
She comes quietly, uncovers his feet, and lies down.
At midnight the man wakes in fear and finds a woman at his feet.
She tells him who she is and asks him to spread his cover over her.
He blesses her and promises to do what she asks, noting that a nearer relative exists.
She lies at his feet until morning and rises before anyone can recognize her.
He tells her to keep her visit secret, then measures six measures of barley into her veil.
She goes back into the city.
She tells her mother-in-law everything the man did and shows the barley.
The older woman tells her to wait patiently to see how the matter turns out.

events_run1: God appears to a man sitting at his tent door in the heat of the day.
The man sees three visitors and runs to meet them, bowing to the ground.
He offers them water, rest under the tree, and bread.
He hurries to have his wife bake cakes and a servant prepare a calf.
He serves the visitors the meal and stands by them as they eat.
The visitors say his wife will have a son, and she laughs to herself as she listens from the tent door.
God asks why she laughed, and she denies it out of fear.
The visitors rise and look toward the wicked city, and the man walks with them to see them off.
The visitors turn toward the city while the man remains standing before God.
The man pleads with God not to destroy the city if fifty righteous people are found there.
He lowers the number step by step, to forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, and finally ten, and God agrees each time.
God goes on his way, and the man returns to his place.
events_run2: God appears to a man sitting at his tent door in the heat of the day.
The man sees three visitors and runs to greet them, bowing to the ground.
He offers them water, rest and food, and they accept.
He has his wife bake cakes and has a servant prepare a calf.
He serves the visitors butter, milk and the calf, and stands by while they eat.
The visitors say his wife will have a son, and she overhears from the tent door.
The old wife laughs to herself, then denies it out of fear when asked.
The visitors rise and look toward the wicked city, and the man walks with them.
Two visitors turn toward the city while the man stays standing before God.
The man asks whether God will destroy the righteous with the wicked.
He bargains step by step, from fifty righteous people down to ten, and God agrees each time.
God goes away and the man returns to his place.
